SHW.rationale: Sherwin-Williams is a durable, high-quality coatings franchise with genuine competitive advantages (4,900+ store network, contractor lock-in, pricing power) and demonstrated cyclicality resilience — Q1 2026 delivered +6.8% YoY revenue growth and +7.5% EPS growth despite declining residential new construction volumes. Gross margin expanded ~80bp YoY to ~49%, and the oil price decline from $100+ to $73/bbl provides a material raw-material cost tailwind for coming quarters. However, the stock is not cheap: PE at 31.7x (mid-range vs 365-day 28-37x band) with a 3.2% earnings yield below the 4.54% 10-year Treasury, meaning the market already prices in continued growth. The balance sheet carries meaningful leverage (debt/equity 2.1x, $9.32B debt), and net margin has slipped modestly to 10.9%. Q2 2026 earnings on July 28 (consensus EPS $3.55, +5% YoY) represent a near-term catalyst that could confirm the oil tailwind is flowing through, but the stock is fairly priced for a quality compounder rather than dislocated. Score reflects solid fundamentals and trajectory (pillar 1) offset by fair-to-slightly-rich valuation (pillar 2), with a modest positive bump from the approaching earnings event (pillar 3).
key_factors: Q1 2026 revenue $5.67B, +6.8% YoY; EPS $2.15, +7.5% YoY — growth in weakest seasonal quarter despite declining new construction volumes
Gross margin ~49.0% (2.78B/5.67B), up ~80bp YoY from ~48.2% — 14th expansion in 15 quarters per qualitative source
WTI crude declined ~27% from $100+ to $73.15 (2026-07-09) — material raw-material cost tailwind for petroleum-derived inputs (TiO2, resins, solvents)
PE diluted 31.7x (365-day range 28.0-37.1x), earnings yield 3.2% below 10-year Treasury 4.54% — fairly priced, not compellingly cheap
Debt-to-equity 2.1x ($9.32B debt, $4.43B equity) — manageable but constrains flexibility; Baa corporate yields at 6.1% elevate refinancing costs
Net margin compressed modestly to 10.9% from ~11.0% typical level (advisory note: actual compression ~10bp, not the 70bp implied by using Jul 2025 peak)
Q2 2026 earnings July 28 — consensus EPS $3.55 (+5% YoY), full-year 2026 consensus $11.77 (+3%), accelerating to $13.38 in FY2027 (+13.7%)
Akzo Nobel pursuit abandoned June 3, 2026 — removed acquisition overhang; Citi reinstated Buy/$355 PT, UBS downgraded to Neutral/$330 PT
Repaint and commercial demand structural moat — 4,900+ store network, contractor lock-in, pricing power from performance risk economics
$772.7M returned to shareholders in Q1 2026 ($575.6M repurchases + $197.1M dividends) — disciplined capital allocation

sources_cited.excerpt: Analysts expect the company to post an EPS of $3.55, up 5% year over year...On June 3, Sherwin-Williams shares gained more than 1% after the company and Nippon Paint announced they were ending their joint pursuit of Akzo Nobel N.V.

Paint Stores Group...reported Q1 2026 net sales of $3,049.9 million, up 3.7% year over year, with same-store sales growth of 2.4%...Volume in the residential new construction end market declined during the quarter, but the segment still grew because repaint and commercial demand more than offset it
The 90-basis-point improvement to approximately 49.1%, the 14th expansion in the last 15 quarters, shows that Sherwin-Williams is not dependent on a particular volume environment to protect margins
The company returned $772.7 million to shareholders in Q1 2026, comprising $575.6 million of share repurchases and $197.1 million of dividends

On June 3, Citi reinstated coverage of The Sherwin-Williams Company (NYSE:SHW) with a Buy rating and a $355 price target...On June 2, UBS downgraded...to Neutral from Buy and reduced its price target to $330 from $385
